set.body:
Measured by running 05-crossnobis-uncertainty.R as written, UNCERTAINTY_NODES=25, reading the script's own instrumentation:

  sampling covariance: 16.2 s total, 0.65 s/node mean

The README Cost section states:

  'rdm_sampling_covariance() evaluates one frame node per call at ~9 s, so it defaults to
   120 nodes (~22 min) and UNCERTAINTY_NODES=all takes ~90 min.'

On this measurement:

  120 nodes    about 80 seconds, not 22 minutes
  577 nodes    about 6.3 minutes, not 90 minutes

An independent reconstruction of the loop body outside the script gives 0.455 s/node, so two methods agree on the order.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY DOC ERROR. That Cost section is the ONLY place a user learns what the error-channel arm costs, and the README explicitly steers them away from it - 'Only 02-04 should be treated as the commit gate.' A user reading that a calibrated error bar costs 90 minutes for one subject's VT mask will not run it. The capability that an entire epic was built to provide is being priced out of use by its own documentation, at more than ten times its actual cost.

I cannot establish when the discrepancy arose. The figure may have been accurate when written and improved since. Either way the current text is wrong against the current tree.

Fix: re-measure and update the Cost section, and reconsider whether 05 still needs to sit outside the commit gate at 6 minutes for a full sweep. Detail and the leak/scaling analysis are on bd-01KZYYQCR3D7NDZQN5DN53AHRC.
set.title: Exemplar README overstates the error-channel arm cost by more than an order of magnitude
